events.title: Jagiellonian University Is Founded
events.description: King Casimir III the Great founded a university in Kraków, Poland. It later became known as the Jagiellonian University and is the oldest university in Poland.
events.significance: It became a leading center of learning in Central Europe, and Nicolaus Copernicus later studied there.

events.title: San Marcos University Is Founded in Lima
events.description: The National University of San Marcos was established in Lima, Peru, by royal decree.
events.significance: It is the oldest university in South America and has shaped the continent's intellectual life for over four centuries.

events.title: Florence Nightingale Is Born
events.description: Florence Nightingale was born in Florence, Italy, to a wealthy British family. She defied social expectations to pursue nursing.
events.significance: Her work during the Crimean War and her use of statistics to improve sanitation helped lay the foundations of modern nursing and hospital care.

events.title: Lindbergh Baby Found Dead
events.description: Ten weeks after being kidnapped, the infant son of aviator Charles Lindbergh was found dead near the family's home in Hopewell, New Jersey.
events.significance: The case gripped the world and led to the federal kidnapping law known as the Lindbergh Law.

events.title: Soviet Union Lifts the Berlin Blockade
events.description: The Soviet Union ended its blockade of land routes into West Berlin. The blockade had begun in June 1948 and had been met by a massive Western airlift.
events.significance: It was an early Cold War standoff that ended without direct war, and it hardened the division between East and West in Europe.
